title: Cost Momentum: Initiative to Reduce Token Unit Costs via Adaptive Batching, KV Prefetching, and Quant Profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Hosted token unit costs have grown 9% QoQ due to longer average sequences and a spike in short-lived interactive sessions. Scope: cross-functional initiative to recover cost by applying three levers: 1) sequence-aware adaptive batching, 2) predictive KV prefetch / prefix caching for recurrent sessions, and 3) per-workload quantization profiles with safety-gated quality checks. Goal: reduce hosted per-token unit cost by 15% (absolute) within the initiative window while keeping 99th-percentile latency within current SLOs and maintaining model quality thresholds. Approach: run a prioritized experiment grid on representative customer workloads (chat, summarization, retrieval-augmented generation), iterate on kernel-level batching heuristics with ENG runtime, and expose per-route quant profiles in the Console for controlled rollouts. Artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Cost+Momentum+PRD, Experiment dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/cost-momentum, Design mockups for rollout UI: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/drive-id, GH runtime prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3577
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate hosted token unit cost reduced by >=15% vs baseline (30-day rolling average)
No regression in model quality: task-level evals show less than 1.5% drop in end-user quality metrics for controlled prompt sets
99th-percentile latency across high-volume routes does not exceed current SLO by more than 5%
Per-route quant profile controls available in Console and feature-flagged for canary rollouts
Experiment dashboard shows statistically significant wins (p<0.05) for at least 3 / 5 representative workloads

metrics_and_targets: Baseline hosted token cost (1M token window): $0.085/token -> target $0.072/token (15% reduction)
End-to-end median latency target: unchanged; 99th-percentile allowable +5%
Quality thresholds: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drop <1.5% on standard eval sets
Adoption targets: 25% of high-volume routes adopt adaptive batching profiles by end of Q2
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quantization causes subtle quality regressions on low-resource languages. Mitigation: keep quant profiles gated per-model + per-route and run language-specific evals before rollout.

Risk: Aggressive batching increases tail latency during bursty traffic. Mitigation: implement latency-aware batching timeouts and soft SLO gates; add automatic fallback to low-batch path on p99 breach.
Risk: KV prefetching increases memory footprint and may affect co-tenancy. Mitigation: implement LRU eviction, per-tenant memory caps, and observability on mem pressure.
Risk: Customers notice cost/quality trade-offs. Mitigation: provide clear console labels, per-route opt-outs, and a 'safety' quality monitor with rollback hooks.

rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): internal-only on canary cluster with synthetic and replayed traffic; monitor p99 and quality (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Pilots): 3 paying customers opt-in via Solutions; run 4-week A/B tests with experiment gates
Phase 2 (Staged Production): Gradual enablement on low-risk routes with automated rollback if quality/latency gates breached
Phase 3 (Broad Rollout): Enable adaptive profiles by default for eligible routes with console opt-out and usage-based rebate for early adopters
experiment_grid: Grid A: batching window (10ms/25ms/50ms) x max-batch-size (8/16/32) on chat workloads
Grid B: KV prefetch TTL (0s/30s/120s) x prefetch probability (0.25/0.5/0.75) for recurrent sessions
Grid C: quant profile A/B tests (int8 symmetric vs per-channel quant) x language buckets
Grid D: combined levers A+B/C for 2 high-volume routes to measure interaction effects
